observations.text: SP, due to incomplete memorization of the critical action procedures, could not state the BOLD FACE steps of the simulated emergency by heart and in sequence, with the result that the IP had to direct the initial actions and execute part of the procedure. Continuation with the Check List/IFG was not accomplished without assistance. Further study of the emergency procedures and of the relevant systems, set as daily assignment, is required.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorized recovery sequence, did not initiate the appropriate emergency procedure when the malfunction was simulated on the navigation leg, with the result that the IP directed the critical action steps and executed part of the procedure. The emergency was not handled effectively without assistance.

SP completed the emergency procedures within the standards of the Training Section; however, the BOLD FACE steps were recited in sequence only after the IP's verbal indications, and the transition to the Check List/IFG was recognized and started with delay. Marginal performance for this block of training - fluency in the critical action procedures is expected to improve with the daily assignment.

SP stated the BOLD FACE steps of the simulated emergency by heart and in sequence, then continued with the Check List/IFG in the standardized sequence without the IP's verbal indications. Two minor errors in the follow-on items were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP stated the critical action procedures by heart, in sequence and without mistakes, and executed the follow-on steps according to the Check List/IFG flawlessly, timely and without IP's intervention. The aircraft limits of Section V of the Flight Manual were observed throughout, and the procedures required when unable to be oriented were applied correctly when the turning point was not identified. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional knowledge and execution of the emergency procedures, stating all BOLD FACE steps by heart and in sequence while maintaining course and aircraft control with negligible deviations. The Check List/IFG was worked in the standardized sequence ahead of the profile, and the SP briefed the IP unprompted on the fuel state, the nearest suitable airfield and the intended recovery, handling the emergency effectively. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized use of the Check List/IFG, did not carry the simulated emergency beyond the critical action steps and omitted the securing items of the affected system, with the result that the IP had to direct and execute the remaining part of the procedure. Knowledge of the relevant systems, set as daily assignment, requires further study.

SP, due to locking onto one malfunction instead of continuing to fly the aircraft, did not maintain course and altitude while working the emergency procedure, with the result that the IP took the controls and completed the procedure. The emergency was not handled effectively without assistance.

SP, due to an unstandardized sequence in the critical action procedures, did not state the BOLD FACE steps in the prescribed order and reversed two items, with the result that the procedure was completed only after the IP's verbal indications. The error was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, did not select the correct Check List/IFG procedure for the simulated system failure on the navigation leg, with the result that the IP's verbal indications were required before the correct procedure was reached. The wrong selection was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP knew and executed the emergency procedures within the desired standards; however, the BOLD FACE recitation was interrupted twice and self-corrected, and the transition to the Check List/IFG was slower than the standardized flow. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed and fluency in the critical action procedures are expected to improve.

SP stated all BOLD FACE steps by heart, in sequence and without mistakes, and executed the follow-on procedure according to the Check List/IFG flawlessly, timely and without IP's intervention. The procedures required when unable to be oriented were applied correctly, with a climb to a safe altitude, the appropriate transponder code and a call to the controlling agency. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled the simulated emergency with exceptional accuracy, completing the critical action procedures by heart while holding course and the Section V limits of the Flight Manual with negligible deviations. The Check List/IFG was worked in the standardized sequence and the SP briefed the IP unprompted on the fuel state, the nearest suitable airfield and the intended recovery. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the critical action procedures for the simulated emergency, could not state the BOLD FACE steps by heart and stopped after the first item, with the result that the IP had to direct the sequence and execute part of the procedure. The emergency was not handled effectively without assistance. Daily study of the procedures and of the relevant systems is required.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft position relative to the planned route, did not apply the procedures required when unable to be oriented and continued on an arbitrary heading, with the result that the IP directed the recovery towards the nearest suitable airfield. Use of the available navigation aids and of the controlling agency as a resource was not initiated without assistance.

SP, due to a non-standardized Check List/IFG flow, did not complete the follow-on items of the emergency procedure in the prescribed sequence and omitted the system-securing steps, with the result that the procedure was completed only after the IP's verbal indications. The omissions were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to failure to shed a secondary task when workload increased, continued map reading while the simulated emergency was in progress and did not work the Check List/IFG in a timely manner, with the result that the procedure was carried through only after the IP's verbal indications. Priority between flying the aircraft and working the procedure was re-established with delay.

SP, due to imprecise recall of the standardized sequence, transposed two BOLD FACE items before completing the critical action procedure, with the result of a minor error that was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The remaining Check List/IFG steps were executed in the prescribed order and the aircraft limits of Section V of the Flight Manual were observed.

SP, due to an unmanaged stress response after the abnormal indication, delayed the start of the critical action procedure and reported the condition to the controlling agency in technical wording instead of plain language, with the result of minor errors that were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The Check List/IFG was thereafter completed in the standardized sequence and the emergency was handled effectively.

SP executed the emergency procedures within the desired standards, stating the BOLD FACE steps by heart and completing the Check List/IFG without IP's intervention; however, the pace of the critical action procedure was at the slow limit of the standard and one step required a second attempt at the correct wording. Marginal performance for this stage of the syllabus - accuracy and speed in the critical action procedures are expected to improve with the daily assignment.

SP demonstrated exceptional knowledge and execution of the emergency procedures, stating all BOLD FACE steps by heart, in sequence and without mistakes, and completing the Check List/IFG flawlessly, timely and without IP's intervention. Course, altitude and the Section V limits of the Flight Manual were held with negligible deviations throughout, and the actions required when unable to be oriented were applied with the fuel state, the divert field and the intended recovery briefed to the IP unprompted. Above end of block MIF achieved.
